intro_html: Chicken thighs braised in a deep red paprika and sour cream sauce over buttered egg noodles. This is a big bowl on purpose: 61 grams of protein and 877 calories of old-world comfort for about $3.36 (at everyday cost). Grandma-level cooking at gas-station-snack pricing.
cost_closing_html: About $3.36 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a paprikash plate the old-school European restaurants price at $17, and they will not send you home with 13 more.
shop_smart: Boneless skinless chicken thighs at $18.37 for 7.5 lb are the value cut of the poultry case, about $2.45 a pound, and they braise better than breast anyway.
This uses a full 14 tablespoons of paprika, so skip the tiny spice-aisle jar and buy the big bottle or the bagged paprika in the international aisle. Same spice, half the price.
Light sour cream finishes the sauce for $2.22 and works exactly like full fat here. Egg noodles round out the plate at about 28 cents a serving.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chicken thighs into large chunks, season with salt and half the black pepper, and toss in the flour until coated.
Brown the chicken in the butter in batches in your biggest pot, 3 to 4 minutes per side. Do not cook it through yet; set it aside.
Cook the diced onion in the same pot until soft, add the garlic, then pull the pot off the heat and stir in the paprika and cayenne so they bloom without burning.
Stir in the tomato paste, sugar, and crushed tomatoes, return the chicken, and simmer covered 20 to 25 minutes until the chicken reaches 165F and is tender.
Boil the egg noodles, drain, and divide them among 14 containers.
Off the heat, temper the sour cream with a ladle of hot sauce, stir it back in with the lemon juice, and ladle the paprikash over the noodles.
portion_html: Weigh the full pot of paprikash, subtract the empty pot number, and divide by 14, splitting the noodles evenly first. Each loaded bowl comes out to about 877 calories and 61 grams of protein.

steps: Flour-coat chunks of seasoned chicken thigh and brown them in butter in batches.
Soften onion and garlic, then bloom the paprika off the heat.
Add tomato paste, sugar, and crushed tomatoes; return the chicken and simmer to 165F.
Boil the egg noodles and divide among 14 containers.
Temper in the sour cream and lemon juice off the heat and ladle over the noodles.
